Rachel — thanks for surface. From rev/ops perspective: we can absorb a modest increase in cap if it's paired with contract levers (insurance, success metrics, usage limits). Two commercial levers to consider:

- A 20% one-time professional services fee to offset incremental risk if cap > 3x ARR.
- Escalating liability tied to deployment milestones (e.g., $1M first 6 months, $3M after production cutover).

I think a $3M cap with a data carve-out + IP indemnity carve-in (limited to claims arising from our code not customer-provided data) is defensible. Would avoid opening general IP indemnity.

Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Final SOW + redlines (liability cap / warranty)

Team —

Reviewed Acme's redlines and Marcus' commercial proposal. Short summary:

1) Liability cap: Acme's ask ($5M) is materially above our standard (typically 1x ARR or $1M floor). Increasing to $3M could be justified only with (a) data & security carve-outs, (b) mandatory insurance (commercial general liability and cyber) and (c) contractual limits tied to usage/pools.

2) Indemnity: Acme's proposed broad IP indemnity (no carve-outs) goes beyond our risk appetite. Our recommended position is to accept indemnity for third-party IP claims but exclude claims arising from Customer Data and any modifications Customer performs. We can include a mutual indemnity clause for third-party claims limited to direct damages.

3) Warranty: Removing consequential damage exclusions materially increases exposure; recommend retaining the warranty limitation. We can consider a narrow warranty on uptime (SLA credits) for the initial 6 months.

Because Acme is strategic and could be a marquee cloud partner, I recommend escalation to execs for a one-time approval if Sales commits to the milestone-based contracting and insurance verification. Drafted proposed counter-language and attached a short memo summarizing risk and proposed mitigations.

If we need exec sign-off, please route the memo and the redline to Aditya for approval. I'm available to brief.

Laura Bennett
VP, Legal & Compliance
Redwood Inference
